name: Chianti

communes: San Casciano In Val Di Pesa

terms: Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita, Italy's top tier. Stricter than DOC, and given only to wines that have been DOC for at least seven years.
A longer-aged wine. Each DOC or DOCG's own rules decide whether it has a Riserva and how long it must age. Chianti Riserva needs at least two years, counted from 1 January after the harvest.

notes: Chianti, led by Sangiovese, has medium-high acidity and medium tannin.
Floral, cherry and light nutty aromas are typical, and basic Chianti shows juicy cherry, plum and raspberry.
Tobacco and leather can emerge with age.

blurb.text: A Tuscan red wine made principally from Sangiovese. It was once tied to a straw-covered flask, the fiasco. Chianti was first given legal boundaries in 1716, for the hills now covered by the separate Chianti Classico DOCG.
